title: Equations & Inequalities
subtitle: Solve One Step
bounds: PROTOCOL 4a, tightened: every equation is one step with whole numbers. Literals under + and − are 1–20, so a + − solution is a whole number 1–40 (at most a sum of two such literals). × and ÷ are times-table facts: factors, divisors and quotients 2–10, so a × ÷ solution is a whole number 2–100. Inequality boundaries 1–20; a choice plugged into x + a is ≤ 20, and one plugged into ax is 1–10, so every check is a fact. No negatives anywhere.

tiers.name: Is It a Solution?
tiers.description: Plug a value in: which one makes the equation true?

tiers.name: Add & Subtract
tiers.description: Solve x + a = b and x − a = b by undoing the step.

tiers.name: Multiply & Divide
tiers.description: Solve ax = b and x ÷ a = b by undoing the step.

tiers.name: Write the Equation
tiers.description: Turn a short story into a one-step equation.

tiers.name: Inequalities
tiers.description: Write x > c or x ≤ c from words, and pick a value that makes one true.

SAME_OP.student: Undo the step with the opposite: + undoes −, × undoes ÷.
SAME_OP.teacher: Applies the equation's own operation to the other side instead of its inverse (x + 7 = 15 gives 22; 4x = 28 gives 112).

VALUE_SHOWN.student: That number is already in the equation. Plug your pick in: is it true?
VALUE_SHOWN.teacher: Picks a number printed in the equation instead of the value of the variable.

SUBTRACTED.student: 4x means 4 times x. Undo times by dividing, not subtracting.
SUBTRACTED.teacher: Reads ax = b as x + a = b and subtracts: 4x = 28 gives 24.

ADDED.student: x ÷ 5 means x split by 5. Undo divide by multiplying, not adding.
ADDED.teacher: Reads x ÷ a = b as x − a = b and adds: x ÷ 5 = 6 gives 11.

WRONG_OP.student: Right numbers, wrong operation. What happens to x in the story?
WRONG_OP.teacher: Writes the story's numbers with the wrong operation (got 6 more gives x − 6 = 15).

SWAPPED.student: Numbers in the wrong spots. Match each number to its job in the story.
SWAPPED.teacher: Swaps the total with the change or group size (x + 15 = 6; 20x = 4).

KEYWORD.student: Key words can trick you. Tell the story with x, then write it.
KEYWORD.teacher: Combines the two printed numbers by a key word ("in all" gives x = 4 × 20) instead of modelling the story.

BOUNDARY.student: < and > leave out the number itself: 4 < 4 is false.
BOUNDARY.teacher: Treats a strict inequality as inclusive and picks the boundary value.

WRONG_SIDE.student: Plug it in: the statement comes out false. Pick from the other side.
WRONG_SIDE.teacher: Picks a value on the wrong side of the boundary (reads < as >, or solves the inequality backwards).

FLIPPED_SIGN.student: Check the direction. Read from the letter: p ≥ 12 means p is 12 or more.
FLIPPED_SIGN.teacher: Reverses the inequality's direction (at least 12 gives p ≤ 12; 9 > n read as n > 9).

STRICT_VS_INCLUSIVE.student: At least / at most include the number (≥ ≤). More / fewer than do not.
STRICT_VS_INCLUSIVE.teacher: Confuses strict and inclusive inequalities (at least 12 gives p > 12).
